sections.title: Life cycle and origin
sections.text: Tartary buckwheat is a cultivated annual native to mountainous parts of central and eastern Asia. It is usually 30–70 cm tall, sometimes reaching 1 m.

sections.title: Flowers and seeds
sections.text: Its greenish-white flowers are often less showy than those of F. esculentum. The angular seeds are more strongly ridged and generally more bitter; they are used for flour, noodles, porridge and infusions.

sections.title: Difference from common buckwheat
sections.text: Fagopyrum esculentum has less strongly ridged seeds and is generally milder in taste. Both are food crops, but the seeds are the main parts eaten.
